era: Japanese Sukiya-zukuri, early 17th century Edo period
room_focus: Zashiki reception hall and tea alcove
inspiration: Edo period tea masters frequently paired the rustic warmth of persimmon tannin wood-stains with symbolic crane motifs representing winter longevity.

shots.name: 1-wide-zashiki-establishing
shots.prompt: An authentic Edo period sukiya zashiki reception room opening to a covered cedar veranda. Smooth igusa tatami mat flooring with sumi black silk borders covers the ground. At the rear, an asymmetrical tokonoma alcove features an unpeeled Kitayama cedar post and hand-plastered juraku earth walls tinted in muted persimmon flesh tones. Sliding shoji screens made of delicate unbleached washi paper diffuse outdoor illumination. Subtle crane-crown red silk accents border the hanging calligraphic scroll. Natural late afternoon daylight at 3200 Kelvin floods softly through timber lattice. Shot on 24mm tilt-shift lens, eye-level from floor seating perspective, f/8, vertical 4:5. Post-and-beam joinery follows strict historic Japanese carpentry without visible fasteners, perfectly straight horizon lines, structural realism.

shots.name: 2-alternate-shoin-angle
shots.prompt: The same sukiya zashiki viewed across the tatami towards the corner shoin built-in desk and low paper-screened window. Earth plaster walls show subtle organic straw fibers and soft persimmon clay undertones. Low floor cushions upholstered in persimmon-dyed linen sit neatly on the reed tatami. The sliding fusuma door panels display minimalist sumi ink wash paintings of roosting cranes on aged paper with matte black iron finger pulls. Gentle 3400 Kelvin ambient daylight filters horizontally through the paper panes. Captured on 35mm lens, positioned fifty centimeters above the floor, f/5.6, vertical 4:5. Every wooden lintel, threshold, and exposed cedar ceiling batten aligns with strict Edo residential proportion, balanced and orderly.

shots.name: 3-mid-tokonoma-detail
shots.prompt: Mid-range architectural detail of the stepped shelving alcove and tokonoma corner within the sukiya room. The natural curved Kitayama log post frames a floating tiered shelf finished in burnished persimmon wood. The textured earthen wall displays hand-troweled juraku clay with deep ochre and warm persimmon warmth. A minimal antique bronze vase holds a single bare persimmon twig with dried fruit, sitting atop a sumi charcoal lacquered floorboard, paired with a hanging silk mounting displaying subtle crane-crest red stitching. Raking side light at 3000 Kelvin emphasizes the textured clay plaster. Shot on 50mm lens, chest height, f/4, vertical 4:5. Realistic interlocking wood joinery, perfectly grounded shelves, historically accurate domestic composition.

shots.name: 4-close-joinery-material
shots.prompt: Extreme architectural macro detail of interlocking Japanese wood joinery where a shoji screen meets the cedar wall post. Fine cedar kumiko geometric lattice holds translucent handmade washi paper dyed with faint kakishibu persimmon tannin. Below, the edge of an authentic green-gold igusa rush tatami mat meets its woven border made from crane-black hemp with a hairline piping of crimson red silk thread. Soft golden hour directional light at 2900 Kelvin rakes across the exposed wood grain and fibrous paper. Photographed on 90mm macro lens, perpendicular angle, f/2.8, vertical 4:5. Flawless surface textures, tactile Japanese craftsmanship, no floating elements, exact historic material accuracy.

hooks: Edo woodcraft dyed with persimmon tannin.
When winter cranes meet Japanese cedar.
reel_script: 0-2s Wide look at a quiet Edo period sukiya zashiki.
2-5s Soft floor-level glide toward the paper shoin window.
5-9s Focus on the asymmetric clay tokonoma and timber shelf.
9-12s Tight macro on persimmon-stained washi and woven tatami.
12-15s Final contemplative view of the entire peaceful hall.
caption:
Persimmon juice has sealed Japanese cedar against age for centuries.

🍵 Style: Edo Sukiya-zukuri, early 17th century
🎨 Palette: Persimmon Flesh · Crane Crown · Unbleached Washi · Sumi Feather Black · Juraku Clay Ochre
🪵 Materials: Kitayama cedar, hand-troweled juraku earth, igusa tatami, kakishibu washi
📐 Focus: Main zashiki → Shoin desk corner → Tokonoma alcove → Kumiko joinery

The unpeeled cedar post makes the whole room feel grounded and quiet.
